newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 15.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Thursday he was removing the foreign ownership restrictions on telecoms companies Optus Communications and Vodaphone Australia. This is seen freeing up Cable and Wirless to take a larger Optus float and smoothing the way for a float of Optus.

Foster's' 40 percent owned Molson Breweries posted a C$2.3 million lower first quarter profit of C$57.1 million early on Friday. Sales rose slightly, but costs linked to an interim agreement with Coors brought profits lower.

Colonial Ltd on Thursday reported a bumper half-year profit and said it could exceed its forecast for full-year 1997 earnings of A$180 million. In its first profit report as a listed company, the life insurance, banking and funds management group said its half-year net profit of A$118 million put it on track to meet, or even better, the forecast given to investors in March.

Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd expected to announce within days a syndicated bank debt facility worth about A$800 million through the Commonwealth Bank of Australia to refinance its existing credit lines, chairman Dick Warburton said late on Thursday. Earlier on Thursday, Sydney Harbour Casino announced a A$7.34 million net loss in the six months to June 30, due to an abnormal loss before tax of A$42.99 million.

Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp said on Thursday it expected a higher net profit, earnings per share and dividend payment in the year to June 30, 1998. Lend Lease earlier reported a net profit increase of 15 percent to A$322 million in 1996/97, compared with the median forecast of A$318 million.

Australia's bigest construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd reported on Thursday a better than expected annual net profit, a surprise special dividend and started a review of options for the group's large cash holdings. Leighton reported a 32.1 percent rise in pre-abnormal net profit to A$86.24 million for the year to June 30, 1997, well above median expectations.

Indonesia succumbed to speculative attacks and floated the rupiah on Thursday, triggering steep declines in the currency and stock prices.The rupiah dove on the news, plunging about four percent or more than 100 points after opening at 2,648/58 against the dollar. Coca-Cola has substantial and growing Indonesian operations.
